title: Entire.io: Working with AI Agents, Without Losing Context
topic: Entire.io — how Entire turns ephemeral AI agent coding sessions into durable, searchable, git-native engineering context: sessions and checkpoints, commit linkage, rewind and resume, multi-agent handoffs, privacy and redaction, and the future of semantic memory for code.

concepts.title: Why Entire Exists
concepts.brief: The problem Entire is solving: AI coding sessions are ephemeral, Git only records what changed, and teams lose the reasoning behind decisions. The shift from human-only SDLCs to agent-heavy workflows. What goes missing when a session ends.

concepts.title: The Mental Model
concepts.brief: The basic conceptual model: sessions, checkpoints, commit linkage, and the separate checkpoint branch. Entire is not just logging — it attaches intent and reasoning to code history.

concepts.title: Checkpoints as a New Primitive
concepts.brief: Checkpoints as the key abstraction. How they function as save points for agent work, and why they matter for traceability, review, and recovery.

concepts.title: Sessions, Commits, and History
concepts.brief: How session history and Git history complement each other: Git tells you what changed, Entire tells you how and why it changed. Why the system keeps metadata separate from the active branch.

concepts.title: Rewind, Resume, and Recovery
concepts.brief: Going back to a known-good state, resuming work later, and handling when an agent goes sideways. Practical workflow benefits of checkpoints.

concepts.title: Multi-Agent and Handoff Workflows
concepts.brief: How Entire supports multiple agents and why that matters. Context becomes transferable — one agent's work becomes another agent's starting point.

concepts.title: Reviews with Intent, Not Just Diffs
concepts.brief: How checkpointed context changes code review. Reviewing prompts, transcripts, constraints, and tool calls to understand the decision path — not just file diffs.

concepts.title: Privacy, Redaction, and Trust
concepts.brief: The tradeoffs of storing agent context in Git: redaction, secret handling, public vs private repos, what teams should think about before adopting. What should never be captured.

concepts.title: Practical Adoption Patterns
concepts.brief: Where Entire fits best: solo developers, teams in feature branches, research-heavy workflows, organizations that need auditability. Usage patterns, not commands.

concepts.title: The Future: Semantic Memory for Code
concepts.brief: The larger vision: Entire as part of a broader agent-memory and reasoning layer. How durable context changes collaboration, onboarding, and long-term code evolution.

summary: A whiteboard-architect's guide to Entire.io — the CLI that turns ephemeral AI agent coding sessions into durable, searchable, git-native engineering context. Covers why agent sessions vanish and what that costs, the core mental model of sessions and checkpoints, how checkpoints work as a new primitive for traceability and recovery, the relationship between session history and git history, rewind and resume workflows, multi-agent handoffs, reviewing agent work with intent rather than just diffs, privacy and redaction tradeoffs, practical adoption patterns for solo devs and teams, and the broader vision of semantic memory for code.
